headline: High: slim’s shell/write/network privileges can conflict with opik’s broad egress and create unsafe cross-agent data handling; prompt-injection risk is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge is documented between opik and slim, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, slim can read/write files and run shell commands, while opik can call REST APIs and has broad egress; if an operator manually passes slim output into opik, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pairwise pathway is therefore low, not none, because manual bridging is possible.
conditions: IF an operator copies slim output into opik prompts or API payloads, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file or terminal transcript is used as an interchange channel, attacker-controlled text can cross agents.
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste template that strips instructions.
Require a human to summarize slim output before sending to opik.
Disable any shared workspace or transcript handoff.
Add a prompt prefix that treats imported text as untrusted data.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim touches filesystem artifacts, environment variables, certificate private keys, and registry credentials, while opik has broad network egress and REST API access. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak sensitive build or container data if slim outputs are forwarded into opik or if both are pointed at the same artifacts. The interaction is plausible in default operator workflows, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF slim processes images containing private keys, registry credentials, or environment variables and its outputs are forwarded to opik, leakage occurs.
IF both agents are run against the same workspace or artifact directory, opik may transmit sensitive contents off-host.
mitigations: Run slim on sanitized images only.
Keep opik and slim in separate directories.
Redact secrets before exporting any slim output.
Block outbound network for opik during sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: opik exposes REST API access and broad egress, but no write filesystem or shell capability is documented. slim has shell, subprocess, filesystem read/write, and broad egress, yet modify_git_state is false and shared-state isolation is documented as no. Because their write surfaces do not clearly overlap, direct capability conflict is limited and low severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file-level contention can occur.
IF an operator uses opik to orchestrate writes through an external API into slim-managed artifacts, conflicts may emerge.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same artifacts.
Serialize any manual handoffs between agents.
Use read-only mounts for opik inputs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands and manipulates container artifacts, while opik can emit REST API calls and broad network traffic. If opik’s outputs are treated as authoritative instructions or facts by slim, errors can cascade into incorrect container modifications or unsafe commands. No verification loop is documented, so the pair presents a medium cascading-error pathway.
conditions: IF opik output is copied into slim command input without review, incorrect actions can be executed.
IF slim consumes opik-generated summaries as authoritative, downstream container changes may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before executing slim commands.
Separate analysis output from command input.
Use a checklist for any opik-to-slim handoff.
Log and diff all proposed actions before execution.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles certificate private keys, registry credentials, environment variables, and vulnerability data, which can trigger residency, retention, or subject-rights obligations. opik has broad network egress and REST API access, so compliance risk arises if those data classes are exported to its backend or logs. The profiles do not document matching controls, so the safer medium classification is warranted.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or vulnerability data are sent from slim into opik-hosted services, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
IF logs from either agent retain certificate keys or credentials beyond policy, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from exported logs.
Confirm retention settings before running.
Use local-only runs for regulated artifacts.
Delete temporary outputs after review.
requires-engineering: document data-processing agreements and residency controls.
